title: Two balloons
logline: Monday. Room 6, 2 AM. A couple fighting. The strip draws the wall and two balloons coming through it, their text cut by the plaster. Wood at the desk, drawing the wall.

panels.composition: The motel hallway, 2 AM. Room 6's door. Two balloons coming through the wall beside it, their text lost in the plaster. WOOD at the hall's end.

image.prompt: razor-sharp brush and ink, a motel hallway at night with two speech balloons emerging through the plaster wall beside a door, their text partly cut off, a night clerk at the hall's end, a flat line beneath
image.notes: Balloons cut by the wall. Letter the fragments after.

panels.composition: The wall. The balloons overlapping. The fragments.

image.prompt: razor-sharp brush and ink, close-up of a plaster wall with two overlapping speech balloons pushing through it

panels.composition: The desk. Wood drawing. The pad: the wall. Two balloons. No words in them; he doesn't put words in other people's balloons.
props: the pad: the wall, two empty balloons

image.prompt: razor-sharp brush and ink, a night clerk drawing a plaster wall with two empty speech balloons on his pad
image.notes: On the pad, the balloons are empty. The strip's rule about strangers' words.

panels.composition: The hallway. Quiet. Room 6's door. One balloon now, small, through the wall. The hum line.

image.prompt: razor-sharp brush and ink, a quiet motel hallway with one small speech balloon coming through a wall beside a door, a flat line beneath

art.line: razor-sharp, confident brush and ink; pristine perspective; crisp silhouettes; zero crosshatch in close-ups
art.palette: dailies: black ink, one spot tone at most. Sundays: wet-on-wet — gray-green moss, fog, rusted tin, bruised dusk
art.paper: bristol for dailies; 140 lb Arches cold-press for Sundays

notes: Two balloons through the plaster. On the pad, empty. '— okay.'
